newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

After hastily convened meetings called by State jockey associations in Sydney and Brisbane, where they jockeys heard that West Australian jockeys had been fined for not racing on Saturday, and that similar action could be taken against jockeys in the eastrn states, champion jockey Mick Dittman said that he and other riders would not tolerate any fines that were imposed. Page 15.

Boxer Kostya Tszyu said yesterday his ambition for this year is to add a second junior-welterweight world boxing title to the one he will defend in Las Vegas in two weeks against Leonardo Mas from Puerto Rico. Tszyu left Australia yesterday to prepare fo the fight. Page 16.

Victorian swimmer Michael Klim won US$150,000 by winning the 100 metres freestyle and the 50 metres butterfly at the World Cup short-course swimming series in Hong Kong on Saturday night. Other winners from the Australian Institute of Sport squad include Matthew Dunn and Adrian Radley. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian cricketer Mark Waugh put Australia in a strong position in their one day international cricket match against the West Indies at the Gabba in Brisbane. Waugh hit 102 from 114 balls and was well backed up by Stuart Law, who hit 93. Australian cptain Mark Taylor only managed 26, yet appeared much more comfortable yesterday. Page 21.

National Racehorse Owners Association chairman Nick Columb said yesterday the association is taking a hard line in response to Saturday's national jockeys' strike. Columb believes that with the jockeys striking and their wish to have their fees upped by 00 per cent, the relationship between the jockey and the owner will change forever. Page 23.

Australian tennis player Todd Woodbridge was able to ditch his label as a doubles specialist yesterday by defeating fellow Australian Scott Draper in the final of the Australian Hardcourt tennis championships at Memorial Drive 6-1, 6-2. Page 23.
THE AGE

Despite an Australian total of 281, the West Indies took the one day international cricket match from Australia in Brisbane, with Brian Lara hitting nearly a run a ball to reach 102. Carl Hooper hit 110 off 108 balls and Jimmy Adams assisted hitting 34 of 39 balls, to see the West Indies win in the 49th over. Page 3.

Despite their 3-0 loss to New South Wales in the national league final, Victoria's women cricketers had reason to celebrate last night, after four state players - all-rounders Zoe Goss and Melanie Jones and fast bowlers Cathryn Fitzpatrick and Charmaine Mson - were picked for the Australian team. Page 4.

The Victorian softball team remains undefeated after its opening three games on the weekend, putting it in good stead to take the Australian softball championship. After a decisive win over the ACT 5-1 on Saturday evening, the team defeated Tasmania 6-0 nd Western Australia 3-1 yesterday. Page 13.
THE HERALD SUN

New South Wales was guaranteed a win in its Sheffield Shield cricket match against South Australia yesterday by claiming four wickets in six overs. The Blues made 415 in their first innings, then set South Australia 452 to win after their second innings,an unachievable target for the inexperienced South Australian side. Page 77.

Two young New South Wales tennis players - Evie Dominkovic and Bryanne Stewart - were picked yesterday as wildcard entries for the Australian Open. The two teenagers are now guaranteed prizemoney of at least A$8,200 for their first appearances at a grandslam event. Page 72.

Australian golfer Greg Norman is on the verge of collecting the largest prizemoney cheque of his career, after surging into the final of the A$4.6 million World Championship of Golf matchplay event in Phoenix, in the United States. Norman defeated Japan' Hisayuki Sasaki 5 and 4 to advance to meet American Scott Hoch in the title decider. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian tennis player Mark Philippoussis has withdrawn from the Sydney International Tennis Tournament after suffering from tendonitis on his right forearm and being advised by doctors not to play. The injury places the Victorian under a cloud for theFord Australian Open and Australian Davis Cup tie against France in early February. Page 29.

Australian water polo coach Erkin Shagaev has called for greater resolve from his players, after the team went down to Greece 7-8 at the fourth and final test at the Sydney Aquatic Centre. The Greek team did not lead the match until the final 43 seconds of play. Page 30.

The UTS Olympic soccer team last night suffered their worst home performance of the season, going down to West Adelaide 4-1 in the Ericsson Cup. There was little fight in the Olympic team, and many fans left the ground before the game was over. Page 35.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
